line: Most people are doing email marketing wrong.
why: The run-up “In today's issue, I'm going to be talking about” is gone, with “I think” and “really”. The claim leads.

line: Most newsletters die at 500 subscribers. Here's why mine didn't.
why: Already sharp: the number up front and a hook that promises the answer.

line: An interesting chart I came across this week shows how much attention spans have dropped
why: “I wanted to share” and “really” are gone, and “basically”. The chart is now the subject.

line: Writing every day is easy. Writing something worth reading every day is not.
why: Already sharp: two short beats, and the contrast is the hook.

line: Your newsletter doesn't need a growth hack. It needs a point of view.
why: Already sharp: two short beats, and the contrast is the hook.

line: My open rate went from 31% to 58% after I changed one thing about my subject lines.
why: Already sharp: the result is up front, and “one thing” opens a gap.

line: As a ghostwriter, I've written over 2,000 posts for founders and CEOs. The ones that perform the best usually have one thing in common
why: One long line is now two beats, and “I've noticed that” went.

line: Most B2B content is boring because it's written to impress other marketers, not to help actual buyers.
why: Already sharp: it opens on the claim and gives the reason, nothing soft to cut.

line: I am now taking on 2 new clients for Q3! DM me if you're interested.
why: “really excited to share that” was run-up. The news now comes first.

line: Your CEO doesn't need to post every day. They need to post one thing that's true.
why: Already sharp: two short beats, and the contrast is the hook.

line: It's important for B2B companies to understand that their buyers are actually people too, and they want to be spoken to like people
why: “really” and “basically” were filler. “actually” stays: it's the point.

line: LinkedIn carousels are the PowerPoint of social media.
why: “Hot take:” is a label readers skip. The claim stands on its own.

line: The exact framework I use to turn a 30-minute founder interview into 12 posts:
why: “Here's” was a run-up. It now opens on “The exact framework”.

line: We increased our client's inbound leads by 312% in 90 days. Here's how:
why: Already sharp: the 312% result comes first and “Here's how:” earns the click.

line: Huge shoutout to @sarahwrites for the amazing feedback on my latest draft. She's the best editor I know
why: “Just wanted to give a” and “honestly” went, so “Huge shoutout” comes first. A full stop splits it in two.

line: I think in 2026, the companies that will win are the ones actually willing to say something interesting.
why: Trimmed “that” twice. “I think” stays: on a forecast it's your stance, not filler.

line: I've lost 30 lbs in the last 4 months without giving up carbs. Here's exactly how I did it in this thread
why: The result stays first, and “I'm going to explain” became “Here's” so the line splits into two beats.

line: You don't need motivation. You need a schedule.
why: Already sharp: two short beats, and the contrast is the hook.

line: Is it actually bad to work out every single day or is that just a myth?
why: “actually” and “just” carry the doubt in the question, so it already works.

line: Hit a 405 lb deadlift today 💪 2 years ago I couldn't lift 135.
why: Already sharp: the lift and the 2-year contrast are up front, and the emoji stays.

line: Most people just need to sleep more and eat more protein, and that's pretty much it
why: “I really think that” and “basically” went. “just” and “pretty much” stay: they carry the meaning.

line: Ran my first marathon today. 4:12:33. Cried at mile 24.
why: Already sharp: short beats with the time and the tears up front.

line: Stop doing cardio on an empty stomach if you actually want to build muscle #fitness #gym
why: “Fitness tip:” is a label readers skip. The advice leads, and “actually” stays.

line: No, you can't out-train a bad diet.
why: Already sharp: a blunt claim with “No” opening it.

line: I just spent 6 hours debugging an issue that turned out to be a missing semicolon. I love programming.
why: The sarcasm is the joke: “I just spent 6 hours” and “I love programming” stay as written.

line: TIL you can use `git commit --fixup` with autosquash and it's a total game changer for keeping a clean history
why: “honestly” was filler. Everything else is your wording and the command stays exact.

line: Most apps don't need microservices. A monolith is probably fine.
why: “Hot take:” is a label readers skip. “probably” stays as your hedge.

line: TypeScript is basically just JavaScript with extra steps, and I'm not sure it's actually worth it for small projects
why: “I think” was a hedge on a claim, so it went. “basically” and “I'm not sure” stay.

line: Rewrote our API from Python to Go. p99 latency went from 800ms to 45ms.
why: Already sharp: the result is up front, with both numbers.

line: What's your go-to stack for a side project in 2026?
why: Already sharp: a short, direct question.

line: `rm -rf /` is not a valid way to free up disk space
why: “Just a friendly reminder that” was a run-up. The command now opens the line.

line: 10 VS Code extensions that will make you a 10x developer:
why: “Here are” and “literally” went, so the number comes first.

line: Junior devs write code. Senior devs delete it.
why: Already sharp: two short beats, and the contrast is the hook.

line: I'm not saying you should never use an ORM, but I am saying you should understand the SQL it generates.
why: “really” was filler. “never” stays: it's the negation your point rests on.

line: Does anyone actually understand how React Server Components work, or are we all just pretending?
why: Already sharp: “actually” and “just” are the joke, nothing soft to cut.

line: Don't deploy on Fridays.
why: Already sharp: four words, nothing to cut.

line: I finally got around to trying out Cursor for the first time and I'm pretty impressed with how it handles large codebases
why: “So”, “I have to say” and “genuinely” went. “pretty impressed” stays: it says quite, not fully.

line: Good design is invisible. Bad design is a support ticket.
why: Already sharp: two short beats, and the contrast is the hook.
